subtitle: How A Buried Stupa Redrew the Faces of the Satavahanas

panels.shot: dramatic three-quarter view of a weathered limestone slab with a royal figure, half-emerging from soil in golden excavation light
panels.action: Kanaganahalli Shilpi kneels in modern excavation trench clothes, one dusty hand brushing soil from a carved royal figure on a limestone slab, the ancient stupa mound and the Krishna river plain stretching beyond.

dialogue.text: For two thousand years the Satavahanas were names in books; at Kanaganahalli, a buried stupa raised their faces from stone and shook the very timeline of an empire.

i18n.hi: दो हज़ार साल तक सातवाहन बस किताबों के नाम थे; कनगनहळ्ळी के दबे स्तूप ने पत्थर से उनके चेहरे जगा दिए और साम्राज्य की टाइमलाइन हिला दी।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot over the dry plains of northern Karnataka, the Krishna river curving past low mounds
panels.action: The camera glides above the fields near Sannati, over scrub and parched earth, pausing on a low, rounded mound ringed by scattered stones and a tiny village shrine.

dialogue.text: On the banks of the Krishna in northern Karnataka, villagers long circled a nameless mound, lighting lamps to a small shrine, never guessing they walked atop a forgotten mahastupa.

i18n.hi: उत्तर कर्नाटक में कृष्णा के किनारे, गाँव वाले सालों उस बेनाम टीले की परिक्रमा करते, छोटी सी वेदी पर दीये जलाते, जाने बिना कि वे भूले‑बिसरे महास्तूप के ऊपर चलते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of archaeologists and workers opening a trench on the mound in the mid-1990s
panels.action: Kanaganahalli Shilpi, here as a present-day site worker with scarf and trowel, crouches in a fresh trench while ASI archaeologists stand nearby with measuring tapes and notebooks, the first courses of brickwork emerging from the earth.

dialogue.text: In 1994, the Archaeological Survey of India cut cautious trenches into the mound; brick by brick, the circle of a great stupa appeared, its broken limestone railings lying where they had fallen.

i18n.hi: 1994 में भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण ने टीले में सावधानी से खंदकें काटीं; ईंट‑ईंट करके महान स्तूप का गोल घेरा उभरा, टूटी चूना‑पत्थर की रेलिंगें जहाँ गिरी थीं वहीं पड़ी मिलीं।

panels.shot: close-up of hands lifting a carved limestone slab from the trench edge
panels.action: Kanaganahalli Shilpi and another unseen worker carefully raise a heavy, curved limestone coping with a carved scene, their fingers coated in red dust, the slab balanced on a wooden support.

dialogue.text: Among the rubble, curved slabs of pale limestone emerged, carved with processions, stupas, elephants, and men with high turbans—railings that once wrapped the great dome in stories.

i18n.hi: मलबे में से हल्के चूना‑पत्थर की घुमावदार पट्टियाँ निकलीं, जिन पर जुलूस, स्तूप, हाथी और ऊँचे पगड़ी वाले पुरुष खुदे थे—वो रेलिंगें जो कभी महागुम्बद को कहानियों से लपेटती थीं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a chiselled Brahmi label above a royal figure on a slab
panels.action: The camera closes in on a smooth band above a carved figure; Kanaganahalli Shilpi gently wipes the surface, revealing neat Brahmi letters incised in a shallow line along the stone.

dialogue.text: Then, on one slab, the stone spoke in letters: a crisp Prakrit label in early Brahmi script, carved above a seated figure like a caption anchoring image to name.

i18n.hi: फिर, एक पट्ट पर पत्थर ने अक्षरों में आवाज़ पाई: शुरुआती ब्राह्मी में साफ प्राकृत लिखावट, बैठे हुए पुरुष के ऊपर, जैसे तस्वीर से नाम जोड़ती कैप्शन।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shilpi and an epigraphist squatting by the slab, intensely focused
panels.action: Kanaganahalli Shilpi crouches beside the slab as an epigraphist leans in with magnifying glass and pencil, copying the Brahmi letters onto a sheet on a clipboard in the hot sun.

dialogue.speaker: the_kanaganahalli_sculptors
dialogue.text: These letters… they fix a face to a king.

i18n.hi: ये अक्षर… ये किसी राजा को चेहरा दे देते हैं।

panels.shot: insert close-up of a scholar’s hand on paper, tracing the inscription while an imagined reconstruction floats above
panels.action: A scholar’s hand traces the Brahmi characters on paper; above the page, ghosted in the air, appears a clear line reading Raja Siri Chimuko Sadavahano, linked by an arrow to the seated stone king.

dialogue.text: The label called him Rāja Siri Chimuko Sādavahano—Chimuka Satavahana—one of the earliest Satavahana rulers, now no longer an invisible name in texts but a carved presence before our eyes.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख ने उसे ‘राजा सिरि चिमुको सादवहनो’ कहा—चिमुक सातवाहन—सबसे शुरुआती सातवाहन राजाओं में एक, जो अब सिर्फ किताबों का अछूता नाम नहीं, हमारी आँखों के सामने तराशी हुई मौजूदगी है।

panels.shot: historic-style wide shot imagining the original railing in place around a gleaming stupa
panels.action: The scene shifts to a reconstructed past: a gleaming white-plastered stupa at Kanaganahalli, its limestone railing complete, the portrait slab in situ, worshippers circling with folded hands under a bright Deccan sky.

dialogue.text: When the stupa was young, Chimuka’s portrait looked out over the circumambulation path, placed among Jataka tales and donors, proclaiming that the Satavahana house now sheltered the Buddha’s relics.

i18n.hi: जब स्तूप जवान था, चिमुक का चित्र जता‑कथाओं और दानियों के बीच परिक्रमा‑पथ पर झाँकता था, घोषणा करता कि अब सातवाहन घर बुद्ध के अवशेषों का रक्षक है।

panels.shot: close-up on the portrait figure itself: a king in profile with ornaments and courtly posture
panels.action: The king on the slab sits in slight profile on a low throne, hair tied and crowned, heavy earrings and necklaces resting on his chest, attendants carved smaller behind him in orderly lines.

dialogue.text: The king is not idealized as a god; he is a man of flesh and cloth, with sober face, ornaments, and attendants, his royal body drawn into the same visual world as the devotees around him.

i18n.hi: राजा को देवता जैसा नहीं, इंसान जैसा गढ़ा गया है; गम्भीर चेहरा, गहने, सेवक, उसका राजसी शरीर भक्तों की ही दृश्य दुनिया में खिंचा हुआ है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot of Shilpi imagining the ancient sculptor at work on the same slab
panels.action: Kanaganahalli Shilpi looks up from the slab, and the scene morphs into an ancient workshop where his ancestral double, bare-bodied and lean, stands carving the same limestone with mallet and chisel.

dialogue.text: Some anonymous sculptor here, two millennia ago, made a daring choice: he placed a living king inside a Buddhist monument, giving the Satavahanas not just power over land but a place in sacred stone.

i18n.hi: किसी गुमनाम शिल्पी ने यहाँ दो हज़ार साल पहले साहसी फैसला किया: उसने जीवित राजा को बौद्ध स्मारक के भीतर बैठाया, सातवाहनों को ज़मीन ही नहीं, पवित्र पत्थर में भी हिस्सेदारी दे दी।

panels.shot: busy interior of an ancient workshop, with Shilpi’s past-self among fellow artisans planning panels
panels.action: The ancient Kanaganahalli Shilpi stands over a rough sketch scratched on a sherd, other artisans crowding around as a monk gestures toward a plan showing donors, kings, stupas and scenes arranged along the railing.

dialogue.speaker: the_kanaganahalli_sculptors
dialogue.text: We carve kings among stories, so future eyes will read patron and path together.

i18n.hi: हम राजाओं को कहानियों के बीच तराशते हैं, ताकि आने वाली आँखें दाता और मार्ग को साथ‑साथ पढ़ें।

panels.shot: montage wide shot of multiple portrait slabs laid out in the excavation storehouse
panels.action: In a modern storehouse, several portrait slabs rest on padded trestles: different royal figures, court scenes, and railing fragments arranged in rows under fluorescent lights and numbered tags.

dialogue.text: Kanaganahalli yielded more than one face: portraits of Satavahana kings, queens, and courts, each with labels, turning what had once been an almost faceless dynasty into a sequence of stone visages.

i18n.hi: कनगनहळ्ळी ने एक से ज़्यादा चेहरों को जन्म दिया: सातवाहन राजाओं, रानियों और दरबार के चित्र, हर एक पर लिखावट, जिससे लगभग बेचेहरा राजवंश पत्थर के चेहरों की कड़ी में बदल गया।

panels.shot: close-up of another inscription mentioning Year 16, with a scholar’s pencil circling the number
panels.action: A scholar’s pencil underlines the Brahmi numerals for sixteen on a photograph of another inscription, the digits clear against the stone while notes in the margin mark its possible link to Simuka.

dialogue.text: One record spoke of a ‘Year 16’ in connection with the Satavahana line; scholars cautiously tied this to Simuka, the dynasty’s founder, giving his reign a relative anchor instead of pure Puranic guesswork.

i18n.hi: एक लेख में सातवाहन वंश के साथ ‘सोलहवें वर्ष’ का ज़िक्र था; विद्वानों ने उसे सावधानी से सिमुक, वंश के संस्थापक, से जोड़कर उसके शासन को पौराणिक अटकल के बजाय एक ठिकाना दिया।

panels.shot: split screen: on one side Puranic lists on palm leaves, on the other excavation plans and stratigraphy charts
panels.action: Ancient palm-leaf manuscripts with Puranic king-lists lie on one side, while on the other side modern stratigraphy diagrams and layer drawings from Kanaganahalli align the stupa’s phases with the inscriptional evidence.

dialogue.text: For centuries, the Satavahana chronology leaned on Puranic lists, full of gaps and contradictions; Kanaganahalli’s layers and labels forced those ghostly sequences to confront bricks, mortar, and dated stone.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक सातवाहन कालक्रम पुराणों की सूचियों पर टिका था, जो खाली जगहों और विरोधाभासों से भरी थीं; कनगनहळ्ळी की परतों और पट्टों ने उन धुँधले क्रमों को ईंट‑गारे और दिनांकित पत्थर से टकरा दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern historian at a desk comparing dates and maps of the Deccan
panels.action: A historian sits amid books, maps of the Deccan spread out, arrows marking Satavahana centers; on the desk lie photographs from Kanaganahalli, Ajanta, and Amaravati, joined by string like a quiet web.

dialogue.text: Akira Shimada and others wove Kanaganahalli into a wider tapestry of early Buddhist sites, numismatics and paleography, using its stupa phases to narrow when the Satavahanas rose across the Deccan plateau.

i18n.hi: अकीरा शिमादा और दूसरे विद्वानों ने कनगनहळ्ळी को शुरुआती बौद्ध स्थलों, सिक्कों और लिपि‑अध्ययन की बड़ी बुनावट में पिरोया, उसके स्तूप के चरणों से अंदाज़ा लगाया कि सातवाहन कब दक्कन के पठार पर उभरे।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of another scholar with magnified Brahmi letters on a computer screen
panels.action: On a computer screen, enlarged Brahmi letters from the Kanaganahalli inscriptions glow; a scholar points out subtle shapes as they compare them with forms from other dated inscriptions in neat columns.

dialogue.text: Yet the stone did not shout exact years; its script styles and archaeological phases only suggested a rough horizon, around the late first century BCE, leaving room for debate rather than final answers.

i18n.hi: फिर भी पत्थर ने साफ साल नहीं पुकारे; उसकी लिपि की शैलियाँ और पुरातात्त्विक परतें बस एक धुंधला क्षितिज सुझाती हैं—करीब पहली सदी ईसा‑पूर्व का उत्तरार्ध—जहाँ बहस है, अंतिम फ़ैसला नहीं।

panels.shot: evocative shot of the stupa ruins at dusk with the river glinting beyond
panels.action: The ruined drum of the Kanaganahalli stupa stands silent at dusk, its exposed bricks casting long shadows, the Krishna river glinting behind under a fading sky, birds wheeling overhead.

dialogue.text: The stupa itself lies broken, its railing scattered, but its measured ruin now pins Satavahana power to a landscape of rivers, trade routes, and monasteries instead of floating in legendary time.

i18n.hi: स्तूप खुद टूटा पड़ा है, रेलिंगें बिखरी हैं, पर उसका नापा‑तौला खंडहर अब सातवाहन शक्ति को नदियों, व्यापार‑मार्गों और विहारों की ज़मीन पर पिन करता है, महज़ दंतकथाओं के समय में तैरने नहीं देता।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shilpi gently touching the portrait slab now in a site shelter
panels.action: Kanaganahalli Shilpi stands in a protective shelter, lightly resting his fingertips on the portrait of Chimuka Satavahana, his face a mix of pride and quiet awe as light filters through wire mesh.

dialogue.speaker: the_kanaganahalli_sculptors
dialogue.text: We carved for the merit of donors; we did not know we carved for historians.

i18n.hi: हमने दानदाताओं के पुण्य के लिए तराशा था; नहीं जानते थे कि हम इतिहासकारों के लिए भी तराश रहे हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot blending past and present: villagers, archaeologists and the imagined ancient processions around the same stupa circle
panels.action: The image layers villagers and archaeologists walking around the ruined base, while faint, transparent figures of ancient devotees and Satavahana royals circle the once-whole stupa in the same path.

dialogue.text: At Kanaganahalli, a single label chiselled above a king binds text to earth, legend to layer, reminding us that sometimes one careful word in stone can reorder centuries of history around it.

i18n.hi: कनगनहळ्ळी में राजा के ऊपर खुदा एक छोटा सा शिलालेख पाठ को धरती से, कथा को परत से बाँध देता है, याद दिलाता है कि कभी‑कभी पत्थर का एक सधा हुआ शब्द सदियों की तारीखें फेर देता है।

title_i18n.hi: कनगनहळ्ळी में दिखता है राजा का चेहरा

subtitle_i18n.en: How A Buried Stupa Redrew the Faces of the Satavahanas
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे दफ़्न स्तूप ने सातवाहनों के चेहरे फिर से बनाए
